subject: Staged deploy rotation & KV-drain playbook for private clusters
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Alex Ramos <ops@acme-labs.com>, Priya Shah <devsec@acme-labs.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-02T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Staged deploy rotation & KV-drain playbook for private clusters

Alex / Priya —

Thanks again for taking time today. Per our call, I sketched a lightweight, low-risk maintenance approach for your private clusters that keeps your version pins intact while allowing critical OS/kernel and runtime security patches to be deployed. Key goals: preserve inference latency SLOs, ensure KV cache safety, and provide a one-button rollback.

High-level proposal (attached: 2026-08-02_patch-timeline.xlsx):
- Stage: run patch on a dedicated staging rack (mirror traffic via traffic-split 5%) and run 2h golden-run (canary inference with pinned model v1.14.2).
- Drain: per-node KV drain before restart; persist KV snapshot to S3-compatible object store; validate cache-hydration on restart.
- Rotate: rolling rotation by AZ, with dual-tagged images (v1.14.2 + patch-label) so we can fall back to original image instantly.
- Fallback: automated rollback-sop.md that re-deploys prior image and restores KV snapshot within 15min target.

Asks for Acme ops:
1) Confirm blackout windows where we cannot touch prod (you mentioned quarter-end reporting week).
2) Provide IAM role that allows our preflight agent to upload KV snapshots to your bucket (least privilege).
3) Agree to the staged cadence: 10% -> 30% -> 60% -> 100% with 30m observation between steps.

Irene/Soojin/Dev — please review the attached checklist and call out any infra gaps (BFD route readiness, firewall egress whitelisting for S3 endpoints, LivePatch vs full reboot tradeoffs).

Thanks,
Karthik
Head of Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

---
Attachments: 2026-08-02_patch-timeline.xlsx (spreadsheet), preflight-checklist.pdf (doc)

From: Alex Ramos <ops@acme-labs.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <devsec@acme-labs.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-02T12:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Staged deploy rotation & KV-drain playbook for private clusters

Karthik —

Appreciate the clear plan. A few quick notes from our side after a quick ops review:
- Blackout: production window is 2026-08-25 00:00 -> 2026-08-28 23:59 (quiet for month-end). Outside that week we have a 6–10pm PST maintenance window on weekdays.
- KV persistence: we can provide a pre-auth'd put-object token for snapshots; will need the ARN pattern to scope it down.
- LivePatch: our kernel team prefers LivePatch for micro-patches; we still require a full-reboot for glibc/major kernel changes. Could you add a decision gate to the playbook that differentiates restart vs LivePatch?

Also, we run cross-AZ Anycast for the load balancer — please include network drain time (we currently rely on 2 min connection drain, but suggestions are welcome).

I’ll loop in our on-call for scheduling once we land on the exact timeline.

— Alex
Senior SRE, Acme Labs

Date: 2026-08-03T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Staged deploy rotation & KV-drain playbook for private clusters

Thanks Alex — good callouts. I added two explicit gates to the playbook:
- Gate A (pre-canary): kernel/no-kernel decision. If LivePatch covers CVE set and vendor certifies no reboot needed, proceed with LivePatch path. Otherwise, route to reboot path and schedule minimal-restart batches (max 5 nodes at a time).
- Gate B (post-canary telemetry): require 3 consecutive 15-min windows with error-rate within baseline AND latency p50/p95 within 2x baseline before advancing stage.

Operational additions I recommend:
- KV drain script v2 that writes snapshot + consistent manifest (sha256) and tags with cluster-id + timestamp.
- Probe harness: a small synthetic runner that hits each model endpoint with a standard prompt set to compare token-perf and deterministic outputs for drift detection.

I attached a short rollback SOP draft (rollback-sop.md) for review — includes early abort criteria and exact CLI commands for image re-tag and KV restore.

Irene
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

Attachment: rollback-sop.md

From: Priya Shah <devsec@acme-labs.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Ramos <ops@acme-labs.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-04T08:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Staged deploy rotation & KV-drain playbook for private clusters

Karthik/Irene —

Security notes from our side:
- We require audit events for: KV-snapshot-upload, image-pull, and node-reboot events. Please ensure these are sent to our SIEM (Splunk) with the cluster-id tag.
- Snapshot storage: encryption at rest is required (SSE-C or KMS). We will only accept uploads to our managed bucket unless you provide a compliant equivalent.
- Access: the preflight agent must authenticate using a time-limited token (OIDC) rather than a static key.

If those are in the playbook I can sign off on the process; otherwise we will block to reduce compliance risk.

— Priya
Director, DevSecOps, Acme Labs

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Alex Ramos <ops@acme-labs.com>, Priya Shah <devsec@acme-labs.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-09T15:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Staged deploy rotation & KV-drain playbook for private clusters — final checklist and schedule suggestion

Alex / Priya —

Thanks for the details. I updated the preflight checklist (attached: preflight-checklist.pdf) to reflect the security and LivePatch branches:
- Auth: OIDC short-lived token flow added; we will exchange a one-time development token for runtime tokens via your STS.
- Encryption: snapshot uploader will set SSE-KMS and include the manifest in the object metadata.
- Network: drain windows increased to 5 minutes to account for long-lived connections; added BFD guard for failover testing in staging.
- Scheduling suggestion: target 2026-09-08 -> 2026-09-10 for staging; production rollout targeted week of 2026-09-21 (outside your blackout).

Next steps:
1) Alex to share bucket ARN for scoping put permissions.
2) Priya to confirm SIEM ingestion endpoint and event schema.
3) We will run the canary on 2026-09-08 and hold for a 2h golden-run, then proceed with 10/30/60/100 cadence.

If Alex signs off on IAM + SIEM items by EOW (2026-08-16), I will convert these to runbooks and schedule a joint dry-run.

— Soojin
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
